characters.appearance: Wind-cut, salt-grey braid, hands scarred by brass polish. Wears her grandfather's coat with the sleeves turned twice.
characters.arc: From keeper of records to author of her own entry.
characters.backstory: Eleven years on the rock; before that, optics school on the mainland.
characters.motivation: Wants: keep the light perfect. Needs: let one imperfect person in.
characters.name: Elena Ferrán
characters.personality: Precise, dry, secretly sentimental about instruments.
characters.secret: She has never once written her own name in the logbook.
characters.voice: Short sentences. Nautical vocabulary for feelings.
characters.wound: Her predecessor — her grandfather — died on the stairs while she was away at school.

characters.appearance: Forearms like bollards, flour on his collar, laughs before he speaks.
characters.backstory: Third-generation boatwright of the village below.
characters.motivation: Wants: an excuse to climb the ninety-two steps. Needs: to be needed for more than bread.
characters.name: Marco Bellandi
characters.personality: Patient, talkative, keeps every promise smaller than he can deliver.
characters.secret: He has read every public logbook entry Elena ever wrote.
characters.voice: Long sentences that end in questions.
characters.wound: A boat he built failed in the '19 storm. No one blamed him; he does.

locations.description: Ninety-two steps, brass and whitewash, the first-order Fresnel lens at the crown.
locations.name: Punta Serena lighthouse
locations.significance: The whole story climbs these stairs. The lens is the third character.

locations.description: One bakery, one slipway, weather talked about like family.
locations.name: The village below
locations.significance: What Elena watches from above and never visits.

logline: A solitary lighthouse keeper who trusts glass more than people must let the village boatwright into her tower — and her ledger of a life — before the great lens, and her certainty, crack for good.

notes.content: First-order: ~2.6 m tall, 920 mm focal length. Cleaning: chamois only on prisms, never rouge on glass — rouge is for the brass ring.
notes.title: Fresnel lens orders

notes.content: Everyone who matters signs the logbook. Elena never has. The romance resolves when she does.
notes.title: Motif: signatures

ch-1.synopsis: Establish Elena's ritual; Marco stays for the fog. The logbook motif opens.

ch-2.synopsis: Spring tides; the storm cracks a prism; she must ask for help.

ch-3.synopsis: The repair, hand in hand. She signs her name.

styleSheet.rule: never abbreviated; the villagers say 'the Punta'

synopsis: Elena keeps the light and the logbook. Marco brings the bread on Thursdays and stays a little longer every week. When the March storm damages the Fresnel lens, they must repair it together before the spring convoys pass the headland. The work forces her to speak; the silence forces him to listen. The light holds. So does the argument with the dark.
theme: Tending something old and fragile — a lens, a heart — is the same discipline.

threads.premise: Storm damage threatens the light before the convoys pass.
threads.resolution: Repaired by hand, together, the old way.
threads.stakes: Ships on the headland; the end of the keeper's post.
threads.title: The lens must survive the spring tides

threads.premise: Thursday bread becomes Thursday repairs becomes Thursdays.
threads.resolution: He signs the logbook as witness; she signs her name.
threads.title: Elena and Marco

timeline.description: Chamois, rouge, and talk. She signs the logbook.
timeline.title: The repair
